sounds.name: Electro Kick
sounds.ref: In the style of the early-1980s electro kick
sounds.blurb: A deep kick with a fast pitch drop: a thump, then a low boom.
sounds.how: A kick is a low drum whose pitch drops very quickly as it is struck. One oscillator tuned near the bottom of TUNE, a fast, wide sweep and a dull filter give the thump; DECAY sets how long the boom hangs on.

steps.title: Tune it right down
steps.why:
- CH 1 TUNE 0.5 (51 Hz): the bottom of the kick, the boom you feel.
- Listen for: a soft low knock below middle C.

steps.title: The thump: a fast, wide drop
steps.why:
SWEEP is DOWN. A very fast sweep across more than an octave is heard as a punch rather than a fall.
- CH 1 SWEEP SPEED 7 (85 ms).
- CH 1 SWEEP RANGE 4 (+14.4 st).
- Listen for: a click-thump at the front of each hit. Slow SWEEP SPEED down and it turns into a tom.

steps.title: A dark boom
steps.why:
- CH 1 DECAY 6 (220 ms): long enough to boom, short enough to stay tight.
- CH 1 WIDTH 1 (0.6 oct): almost no filter sweep, so the kick stays round.
- Listen for: a clean, deep kick.

context.ch1.sweepSpeed: In this sound: the punch of the kick.
context.ch1.decay: In this sound: how long the boom hangs on.

tweaks.hear: From a short, tight kick to a long, booming one.
Deeper or punchier; on small speakers the higher kick carries better.

sounds.name: Noise Hats
sounds.blurb: Ticking hi-hats from a short burst of bright noise, louder on the accented notes.
sounds.how: OSC MODE F is noise alone, and TUNE moves the filter, so a high TUNE leaves only the hiss at the top. A very short decay turns it into a tick; how hard each key is played sets how loud and bright it is.

steps.title: Noise only
steps.why:
- CH 2 OSC MODE F: noise, no oscillators.
- CH 2 TUNE 9.5 (2.1 kHz): the filter sits an octave above that, so only the top of the hiss is left.
- CH 2 SWEEP OFF: noise has no pitch to sweep.
- Listen for: a thin hiss from middle C up.

steps.title: Make it a tick
steps.why:
- CH 2 DECAY 2.5 (27 ms): a closed hat, gone almost at once.
- CH 2 WIDTH 7 (4.2 oct): bright on the strike.
- Listen for: the accented off-beats standing out from the quieter sixteenths. Raise DECAY to 5 for an open hat.

context.ch2.decay: In this sound: closed (short) or open (long) hats.

tweaks.hear: From a tight tick to an open, washy hat.
From a dull shaker to a sizzling hat.

sounds.name: Synth Vibes
sounds.blurb: A soft, ringing mallet tone with a slow vibrato, tuned to the key with FINE.
sounds.how: Mode C mixes the two oscillators, which sit a little apart (440 and 450 Hz on the original), so they beat slowly against each other like a vibraphone’s tremolo. A long decay with the sweep off lets it ring, and a gentle triangle LFO adds vibrato.

steps.title: Two oscillators, a little apart
steps.why:
- CH 2 OSC MODE C: both oscillators mixed, oscillator 1 a little quieter.
- CH 2 TUNE 6.5 (615 Hz) and FINE 7 (+0.4 st): FINE trims the pitch to the key of the music once TUNE is close.
- CH 2 SWEEP OFF: a mallet does not bend.
- Listen for: a pure tone with a slow shimmer from the two oscillators beating.

steps.title: Ring like a bar
steps.why:
- CH 2 DECAY 9 (1.4 s): the long ring of a metal bar.
- CH 2 WIDTH 3 (1.8 oct): a soft mallet, not a hard one.
- Listen for: notes that overlap and fade slowly.

steps.title: A slow vibrato
steps.why:
- CH 2 LFO WAVE triangle: a smooth swing.
- CH 2 LFO SPEED 5 (4.47 Hz), DEPTH 2.5 (+0.8 st): a gentle wobble, like the vibraphone’s motor.
- Listen for: the pitch swaying as each note rings. Switch the LFO OFF to hear how still it was.

context.ch2.fine: In this sound: trims the tuning to the key.
context.ch2.lfoDepth: In this sound: the depth of the vibrato.

tweaks.hear: From a lazy sway to a fast, nervous shimmer.
The same notes turn to struck metal.

sounds.name: Thin Metal
sounds.blurb: A clanging, hissing hit like a struck sheet of metal, for industrial and electro beats.
sounds.how: Mode E is the FM of mode B with noise added: the inharmonic clang and a hiss on top. A small, fast sweep gives the strike an edge, and a bright WIDTH lets the hiss through before the filter closes.

steps.title: FM and noise
steps.why:
- CH 2 OSC MODE E: oscillator 1 bends oscillator 2 for the clang, and noise is mixed in.
- CH 2 TUNE 7 (757 Hz).
- Listen for: a harsh, hissing clang from middle C up.

steps.title: A sharp edge
steps.why:
- CH 2 SWEEP SPEED 8 (53 ms), RANGE 1 (+3.6 st): a tiny, fast drop at the strike.
- Listen for: a crisper front to each hit.

steps.title: Bright, then gone
steps.why:
- CH 2 DECAY 6 (220 ms).
- CH 2 WIDTH 6 (3.6 oct): the strike opens the filter wide, so the hiss sizzles before it darkens.
- Listen for: a metallic smack. Lower WIDTH for a duller, more distant one.

context.ch2.mode: In this sound: E, FM plus noise.

tweaks.hear: From a dustbin lid to a small, ringing plate.

sounds.name: Square Trill
sounds.ref: A drum that trills between two notes
sounds.blurb: A ringing tone that flips quickly between two pitches a minor third apart.
sounds.how: The square LFO jumps the pitch between two levels instead of swinging smoothly. At LFO DEPTH 5 the jump is three semitones up and down from TUNE, so the drum trills like a bird or an old telephone.

steps.title: A held tone
steps.why:
- CH 1 TUNE 5 (330 Hz).
- CH 1 SWEEP OFF.
- CH 1 DECAY 8.5 (1.0 s): the trill needs time to be heard.
- Listen for: a plain, ringing tone below middle C.

steps.title: The square LFO
steps.why:
- CH 1 LFO WAVE square: the pitch jumps instead of gliding.
- CH 1 LFO SPEED 6 (7.25 Hz): about seven flips a second.
- CH 1 LFO DEPTH 5 (+3 st): three semitones either way.
- Listen for: the trill. Switch to the triangle and it becomes a siren.

context.ch1.lfoWave: In this sound: square, which jumps between two pitches.

tweaks.hear: From a slow two-note call to a buzzing warble.

sounds.name: Power-Up Blip
sounds.blurb: A short blip that leaps up in pitch, the sound of collecting something in an arcade game.
sounds.how: SWEEP UP starts each hit at TUNE and rises by RANGE. Fast and wide, it reads as a cheerful blip rather than a drum.

steps.title: Sweep up
steps.why:
- CH 2 SWEEP UP: the pitch rises from where it is struck.
- CH 2 SWEEP SPEED 6 (140 ms), RANGE 7 (+25.2 st): two octaves up, quickly.
- Listen for: little upward chirps from middle C up.

steps.title: Pitch and length
steps.why:
- CH 2 TUNE 6 (500 Hz): where the blip starts.
- CH 2 DECAY 5 (120 ms) and WIDTH 5 (3.0 oct): short and bright.
- Listen for: a crisp, chirpy blip.

context.ch2.sweep: In this sound: UP, a rising sweep.

tweaks.hear: From a small chirp to a leap of three octaves.
